snapshot.text: Armenia is moving from a mostly out-of-pocket model toward mandatory universal health insurance, which started in phases on 1 January 2026. Main challenges are heavy private spending, limited public funding, and whether costs stay affordable as projections rise for 2027. Life expectancy is about 77 years.

priorities.title: Phased universal health insurance expansion
priorities.text: Cabinet has approved draft amendments extending universal insurance from 1 January 2027 to employees earning up to 200,000 drams monthly, with shared state and employer contributions.

priorities.title: Hospital tariff and pay revision
priorities.text: The ministry is revising hospital service prices, which often exceed state coverage levels, and has fully revised pediatric surgical pricing. Adult surgical tariffs are also flagged for revision.

priorities.title: People-centred care in 2026-2031 programme
priorities.text: The ministry is planning health measures under the government's 2026-2031 programme, stressing people-centred care, continued infrastructure development and a healthy society.

netherlands.text: Armenia and the Netherlands signed a strategic partnership declaration in March 2025. Their foreign ministers said both sides plan to deepen cooperation in healthcare, alongside infrastructure, agriculture and floriculture.
